Start My Plan Below

What to bring to your first meeting

Bring what you can find — you do not need everything on this list to get started.

  • Your loved one’s full legal name and date of birth
  • Social Security number for the death certificate
  • A recent photograph for the program and display
  • Clothing for your loved one, if you have chosen it
  • Military discharge papers (DD-214), if they served
  • Cemetery information, if a plot is already owned
  • Any pre-arrangement papers, if a plan already exists
  • Names for the obituary — spouse, children, parents

Start your plan right now

Answer what you know and skip what you don’t. In about two minutes you will have a clear summary to bring to the chapel or share with family.

Cremation Services

        
Cremation, with the same Cole care

        
More families choose cremation today than ever before. It can be as full and personal as any funeral — a visitation, a service, favorite music and flowers — or as simple and quiet as your family wishes. Either way, your loved one is in our family’s care from the moment they come to us.

      


      

        

          Cremation with a funeral service
          A full service at either chapel first — visitation, family hour, music, and readings — with cremation following.
        

        

          Cremation with a visitation
          Time for family and friends to gather and say goodbye together, before a private cremation.
        

        

          A memorial gathering, afterward
          Cremation first, then a gathering at the chapel, at church, or at home — planned at your family’s pace.
        

        

          Simple cremation
          A direct, dignified cremation with no service, for families who prefer something small and private.
        

      


      

        
Questions families ask us

        

          Can we still have a visitation and funeral with cremation?
          
Yes. Many families hold a full visitation and funeral first, exactly as they would with a burial, and cremation takes place afterward. Choosing cremation never means giving up time together.

        

        

          What happens after the cremation?
          
Your loved one’s ashes are returned to your family. From there, families choose an urn for keeping at home, burial in a cemetery, placement in a niche, or a scattering in a place that mattered to them. We will walk through each choice with you.

        

        

          Can cremation be planned ahead?
          
Yes, and many Detroit families do exactly that. Use the starter form on this page to write down your wishes, then bring your summary to either chapel and we will keep it safely on record.

        

        

          How do we get started?
          
Start with the planning form — choose “Cremation” as your type of service — or come to either chapel. No appointment is needed to begin, and we will explain each step before you decide anything.

        How Pricing Works
      

    

  


  
  

    

      

        
Clear Pricing

        
Prices in writing, before you decide

        
Too many funeral home sites hide their prices entirely. Ours will not. Here is exactly how pricing works with our family, so there are no surprises on a hard day.

      

      

        

          
A written price list

          
At your first meeting you receive our General Price List in writing — every service and charge itemized — and you may take it home with you.

        

        

          
Only what you choose

          
You pick each service and item yourself, for burial or cremation alike. Nothing is bundled in or added without your family’s say-so.

        

        

          
A total before you commit

          
Before arrangements are final, you receive a written statement of everything you selected and its total cost. No pressure, and no obligation to decide on the spot.

Our History

        
Four generations of the Cole family

      

      

        
James H. Cole Home for Funerals was established in 1919, and for 107 years our family has served the families of Detroit. What began as one funeral home has been carried forward, generation by generation, by the same family and the same promise: to treat every person who comes through our doors as we would our own.

        
Today, as a fourth generation, family owned home, we remain rooted in the neighborhoods we serve. Generations of Detroit families have trusted us in their hardest moments, and we work every day to be worthy of that trust.
